answer: At each monthly summit, the velvet market pays grants only to keys served by its public queue that month. Validators anchor each filing to its signed key and advance one key per day without banking unused turns. A served position pays once, cannot move to another key and expires at the summit. An honest applicant consumes 1 queue-day; paying 1,000 aliases consumes 1,000 queue-days across summits under one shared queue. Farms can still crowd out traders by joining early, but flooding the queue cannot advance the payout clock. Honest traders also face that wait.
